subject: Proposal: Senior IC band definitions and geo adjustments
messages:
From: Ben Harper <ben@pearlcomp.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Senior IC benchmarking + draft proposal

Vivek,

Attached is the executive summary from our January market survey and the preliminary banding proposal for Senior ICs (S3-S5) across US/EMEA/APAC. Key highlights: 
- US market median for Senior IC (S4-equivalent) rose ~4.5% YoY; tech hubs show higher carry.
- Geo spread: SF/NY ~+18% vs remote regional hubs; W. EU ~ -6% vs US; India/SEA ~ -45% vs US median.
- Total comp sensitivity is strong to equity bands for S4+.

I pulled a simple recommendation for Redwood: tighten the S3->S4 delta to 8% (from 12%) to reduce compression and introduce a modest regional multiplier for Bay Area/NYC of +12%. We included spreadsheets with decile breakdowns.

Attachments:
- 2026-02_pearl_survey_summary.pdf (summary, 6 pages)
- market-benchmarks-2026.xlsx (raw tables)

If you want, Luke at Benchmarks Inc. can run a peer-filtered view (startup vs scale) next week.

Best,
Ben Harper
Principal, Pearl Compensation Consulting

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Senior IC benchmarking + draft proposal

Marissa / Neha — filing this here for feedback. Ben's attached proposal has a few concrete asks: tighten level deltas and add geo multipliers for BA/NYC. I've also attached the internal draft band doc (senior-ic-band-draft.docx) so you can see how we currently map S3-S5.

Questions we need to resolve this week for offers and the upcoming hiring plan review: 
- Are we comfortable introducing a Bay Area premium (12%) for open offers this quarter?
- Do we tighten leveling (S3->S4) now or phase it over two quarters?
- Any blockers from a comp governance / budget perspective?

I want to present a recommendation to the leadership hiring committee on Feb 19; short turnaround.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Senior IC benchmarking + draft proposal

Vivek — thanks for flagging. Quick thoughts after a read-through:
- I support a narrower S3->S4 gap (8%) for progression clarity; it reduces pay compression at S4 where market is tight.
- Bay Area premium: +12% is reasonable for total comp but that creates inconsistencies for internal equity if we keep current offer cushions. Suggest we implement as an "offer-region adjustment" only for external hires, not internal promotions, and revisit during the annual calibration.
- On phasing: prefer a split approach — adopt the leveling change immediately for new offers (date-of-offer rule) and defer retroactive adjustments to promotions until Q3 budget cycle.

Attachments: updated draft band doc (I added an offer-note) — please see the "Offer-region adjustment" section.

Also, hiring committee will expect an ask line: incremental OPEX for these band changes. I'll work with Finance to estimate headcount-dollar impact if we adopt the BA premium across open reqs.

Marissa
Director, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Senior IC benchmarking + draft proposal

Folks — a few governance and procurement notes from my side: 
- Any geo-premium that affects offer letters will need revised offer templates and a short comms plan for candidates and hiring managers. Legal has flagged that we must be explicit about "region of work" vs "residence" for distributed roles.
- Finance requests a conservative estimate: apply the BA premium only to open SaaS/Platform reqs for next 90 days; if hiring pace accelerates, we'll need a reforecast.
- For equity: recommend we keep the current equity-multipliers for S4+ for now; moving that is higher impact and should be a separate proposal.

One more ask: Markus, can you confirm if there are any comp band constraints from the people ops tools (salary bands enforced in Workday / job templates)? I want to make sure we can operationalize quickly if we adopt the offer-region adjustment.

Neha Kapoor
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Harper <ben@pearlcomp.com>, Luke Sanders <luke@benchmarks.inc>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Senior IC bands: decision and immediate next steps

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary of decisions and action items for the hiring committee presentation (Feb 19):
1) Leveling change: adopt S3->S4 delta = 8% for new offers effective immediately (date-of-offer). Promotions remain on current cadence; retro adjustments to promotions deferred to Q3 review.
2) Bay Area / NYC premium: implement a +12% offer-region adjustment for open roles sourced in CA/NY markets for the next 90 days; Finance to reforecast if hiring pace changes. This will be applied to base+bonus to calculate cash target.
3) Equity: no changes for now. Separate follow-up item to explore equity multipliers for S4+ in Q2.
4) Operationalization: Neha to confirm Workday constraints and update offer templates by Feb 24. Marissa to produce headcount-dollar impact estimate (OPEX delta) by Feb 18 EOD. Ben / Luke — please stand by in case we need a peer-filtered comparison for the hiring committee.

I've attached the final slide (light) we'll show at the committee and the marked band doc. If no objections by EOD tomorrow I'll finalize the deck and submit to Leadership.

Thanks — Vivek
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
